traditional it infrastructure is often fixed: the organization buys servers and decides how many resources it needs. cloud infrastructure is flexible: resources can be allocated, adjusted and released as requirements change. this dynamic management is the central idea of the topic. 6.1 meaning of dynamic infrastructure dynamic infrastructure is an it infrastructure in which computing resources such as servers, storage and networks can be allocated, adjusted and released according to changing requirements. in simple words: instead of keeping the same amount of resources all the time, an organization changes them whenever needed. example: a shopping website normally gets 1,000 visitors a day, but 50,000 during a festival sale. cloud infrastructure provides extra servers for the increased traffic and releases them when demand falls. 6.2 what is cloud infrastructure? the hardware and software resources required to provide cloud services. main components: servers: process requests and run applications. storage: stores files, databases and other information. networking: connects users, servers and cloud services. virtualization: creates virtual resources from physical hardware. management software: controls resource allocation, monitoring and provisioning. management software (provisioning, monitoring, allocation) virtualization (creates virtual resources) servers process requests storage files and databases networking connects everything figure: components of cloud infrastructure 6.3 how does dynamic infrastructure work? monitor demand: the system monitors cpu, memory and network traffic. allocate resources: additional resources are provided when required. scale infrastructure: server capacity or storage is increased or decreased. release resources: unnecessary resources are released when demand falls. this process can be automated using cloud management tools. 1. monitor demand 2. allocate resources 3. scale up or down 4. release unused resources repeats continuously, can be automated figure: working of dynamic infrastructure 6.4 role of virtualization and automation virtualization: separates computing resources from physical hardware and creates virtual machines or other virtual resources. automation: automatically provisions, configures and manages resources according to predefined requirements. together they help providers deliver resources quickly and efficiently. 2 servers normal day 1,000 visitors 20 servers festival sale 50,000 visitors 2 servers after sale resources released add release figure: dynamic infrastructure: resources follow demand (example numbers) 6.5 benefits of dynamic infrastructure flexibility: resources change according to requirements. scalability: supports increasing workloads. better resource utilization: fewer idle resources. cost efficiency: avoid paying for unused resources when pricing is usage-based. faster deployment: new computing environments created quickly. automation: less manual infrastructure management. 6.6 exam-ready answer q. what is cloud and dynamic infrastructure? dynamic infrastructure is an it infrastructure in which computing resources such as servers, storage and networks can be allocated, adjusted and released according to changing requirements. cloud infrastructure consists of servers, storage, networking, virtualization and management software. dynamic infrastructure works through these steps: monitoring resource requirements. allocating resources according to demand. increasing or decreasing computing capacity. releasing unnecessary resources. virtualization and automation play important roles in managing it. example: an e-commerce website uses extra cloud servers during festival sales and reduces them when traffic decreases. thus, dynamic infrastructure makes cloud computing flexible, scalable and efficient. youtube videos (hindi) jayesh umre: cloud dynamic infrastructure. best match, covers this exact computing characteristics yellow yellow priority : moderate detail, important fundamentals why important? cloud computing has special features that distinguish it from traditional computing. they explain how resources are accessed, shared, increased or decreased, and billed. the most important exam point is the five essential characteristics defined by nist (national institute of standards and technology). learn these five carefully. 7.1 meaning cloud computing characteristics are the special features that describe how cloud services work and how they provide resources to users. in simple words, they explain what makes cloud computing different from traditional computing. according to nist, cloud computing has five essential characteristics. 7.2 five essential characteristics red important: learn all five 1. on-demand self-service users obtain computing resources such as servers and storage whenever needed, without contacting the provider’s staff. example: you create a virtual server on aws yourself through its website. remember: the user requests the resource and the cloud platform provides it automatically. user requests a server request cloud platform self-service portal provision virtual server created automatically no provider staff needed: the platform does it automatically figure: on-demand self-service 2. broad network access cloud services are available over a network and can be accessed through different devices using standard network mechanisms. example: google drive from a mobile phone, laptop, tablet or desktop. cloud service mobile phone laptop tablet desktop figure: broad network access: one service, many devices 3. resource pooling the provider combines its computing resources (servers, storage, processing power, network resources) into a shared pool and provides them to multiple customers according to their requirements. example: one provider uses a large shared infrastructure to serve different companies. remember: multiple customers share a common pool, while their environments are logically separated. shared resource pool servers, storage, processing power, network company a (logically separated) company b (logically separated) company c (logically separated) figure: resource pooling: many customers share one pool 4. rapid elasticity resources can be quickly increased or decreased according to changing demand. example: a shopping site normally has 1,000 visitors a day, 50,000 during a festival sale. the cloud adds resources for the extra traffic and reduces them later. remember: scale up = increase resources, scale down = decrease resources. low demand few resources high demand more resources low demand few resources scale up scale down figure: rapid elasticity: scale up and scale down 5. measured service resource usage is monitored, measured and reported by the provider. customers can track consumption and are often charged according to use. example: if you use 100 gb of cloud storage, the provider measures it and calculates charges by its pricing model. remember: it works somewhat like an electricity meter. usage 100 gb storage used provider meters monitors, measures, reports measured bill charged by pricing model works like an electricity meter figure: measured service cloud computing 1. on-demand self-service 2. broad network access 3. resource pooling 4. rapid elasticity 5. measured service figure: five essential characteristics of cloud computing (nist) 7.3 additional common characteristics some sources list more than five. they are useful extras, but when a question asks for the five essential characteristics, nist’s five are the standard answer. additional characteristic simple meaning multi-tenancy multiple customers use shared infrastructure with logical separation virtualization creates virtual computing resources from physical hardware automation performs resource management tasks automatically reliability helps provide consistent services security protects data, applications and infrastructure flexibility users choose resources according to their needs 7.4 characteristics vs benefits do not confuse these two terms. characteristics benefits describe how cloud computing works describe what advantages it provides resource pooling better resource utilization rapid elasticity easy scalability measured service usage-based cost management broad network access accessibility on-demand self-service faster resource provisioning characteristic (how it works) benefit (what you gain) on-demand self-service faster provisioning broad network access accessibility resource pooling better utilization rapid elasticity easy scalability measured service usage-based cost figure: characteristics vs benefits 7.5 exam-ready answers 1-mark question q. name any two characteristics of cloud computing. on-demand self-service. resource pooling. 5-mark question q. explain the five essential characteristics of cloud computing. according to nist, cloud computing has five essential characteristics: on-demand self-service: users obtain resources whenever required without contacting the provider. broad network access: services are accessed through devices such as laptops, mobiles and tablets. resource pooling: resources are shared among multiple customers according to their requirements. rapid elasticity: resources are quickly increased or decreased according to demand. measured service: resource usage is monitored and measured for transparency and billing. these characteristics make cloud computing flexible, accessible and efficient. cloud computing tutorialspoint: cloud computing characteristics nist: the nist definition of cloud computing (sp 800-145) topic 4. security in a public cloud yellow yellow priority : related topic, moderate preparation why study this? the previous-paper analysis has related 15-mark questions: explain the security concerns and challenges in a public cloud and write a short note on security in a public cloud . it is part of the official unit ii syllabus. 4.1 what is public cloud security? definition: public cloud security refers to the policies, technologies and security measures used to protect data, applications, networks and infrastructure hosted in a public cloud. when an organization stores data or runs applications on a public cloud such as aws, microsoft azure or google cloud, it must protect them from unauthorized access, data theft and cyberattacks. example: an online shop stores customer details, passwords and payment-related information on aws. it must ensure: only authorized employees can access customer information. hackers cannot steal sensitive data. data stays protected while being transferred. applications remain available to customers. 4.2 main security goals: cia triad cia triad confidentiality (privacy) integrity (accuracy) availability (accessibility) figure: cia triad: the three main security goals goal meaning example confidentiality only authorized people can access information customer data visible only to authorized employees integrity data must not be changed without permission nobody can secretly modify transaction records availability services and data accessible when needed an online shop stays available to customers remember: confidentiality = privacy, integrity = accuracy, availability = accessibility. 4.3 major security concerns in a public cloud public cloud threats data breach data loss unauthorized access insecure apis account hijacking insider threats privacy and compliance figure: major security concerns in a public cloud 1. data breach unauthorized people gain access to confidential information. example: a hacker accesses a cloud database and steals customer details. protection: encryption, strong passwords, access controls. 2. data loss information is accidentally deleted, corrupted or becomes unavailable. example: an employee accidentally deletes important files in cloud storage. protection: regular backups, versioning, disaster recovery. 3. unauthorized access someone accesses cloud resources without proper permission. example: an attacker uses a stolen employee password to enter a company’s cloud account. protection: multi-factor authentication (mfa), strong passwords, role-based access control. 4. insecure apis an api (application programming interface) lets different software communicate. cloud services use apis to manage resources and exchange data, so poorly secured apis can be exploited. protection: api authentication, authorization, encryption and proper validation. 5. account hijacking attackers take control of a legitimate user’s cloud account. example: an attacker steals login credentials and uses them on a company’s cloud dashboard. protection: mfa, secure login practices, suspicious-login monitoring. 6. insider threats a threat from someone who already has legitimate access, such as an employee or administrator. example: an employee intentionally downloads confidential information and shares it with outsiders. protection: limited permissions, activity monitoring, audit logs. 7. privacy and compliance issues organizations may have to follow laws and regulations about personal and sensitive information. example: customer data stored in a location that does not meet applicable data protection requirements. protection: follow relevant regulations, know where data is stored, review the provider’s compliance arrangements. 4.4 security measures used in a public cloud security measures encryption authentication authorization access control firewall backup monitoring auditing mfa figure: security measures used in a public cloud security measure what it does encryption converts readable data into an unreadable form without the required key authentication verifies the identity of a user authorization decides what an authenticated user may do access control restricts access to authorized users and resources firewall controls incoming and outgoing network traffic by security rules backup keeps additional copies of important data monitoring observes cloud activity and helps detect suspicious behavior auditing records and reviews activities to find security problems mfa requires more than one verification method to log in important difference: authentication = who are you? authorization = what are you allowed to access? logging in with a username and password is authentication. being allowed to view a file but not delete it is authorization. login (user, pass) authentication who are you? authorization what can you access? access view: yes delete: no figure: authentication vs authorization 4.5 shared responsibility model red important concept security responsibilities are divided between the cloud service provider (csp) and the cloud customer . the provider protects the underlying cloud infrastructure, while the customer protects the resources and configurations they control. customer: security in the cloud data, user accounts and permissions, access controls, applications, customer-controlled configurations cloud provider: security of the cloud physical data centre, servers and hardware, physical networking, virtualization, infrastructure maintenance figure: shared responsibility model responsibilities of the cloud provider physical data centre security. physical servers and hardware. physical networking infrastructure. underlying virtualization infrastructure. maintaining the cloud infrastructure. responsibilities of the cloud customer protecting their data. managing user accounts and permissions. configuring access controls. securing applications. protecting customer-controlled systems and configurations. the exact division changes with iaas, paas or saas. an iaas customer manages the operating system, whereas a saas provider manages much more of the software stack. 4.6 advantages of public cloud security centralized security: controls managed through a central cloud platform. scalability: security resources adjust as workloads grow. monitoring: cloud activity can be monitored continuously. backup and recovery: supports data backup and recovery. security tools: providers offer tools for encryption, access control and threat detection. however, a reputed provider does not automatically make your cloud environment secure. incorrect configurations and weak access controls can still create serious risks. 4.7 exam preparation 1-mark questions what is public cloud security? protecting data, applications and infrastructure hosted in a public cloud from security threats. what is a data breach? unauthorized access to confidential information. what is mfa? multi-factor authentication: multiple verification methods confirm a user’s identity. what is a firewall? a security system that controls network traffic according to predefined rules. what is the shared responsibility model? a model dividing cloud security responsibilities between the provider and the customer. 5-mark question q. write a short note on security in a public cloud. public cloud security refers to protecting data, applications and infrastructure hosted on public cloud platforms. its main objectives are confidentiality, integrity and availability. major concerns: 1. data breaches. 2. data loss. 3. unauthorized access. 4. insecure apis. 5. account hijacking. 6. insider threats. 7. privacy and compliance issues. these risks are reduced using encryption, authentication, authorization, firewalls, backups, mfa and continuous monitoring. cloud security follows a shared responsibility model: the provider protects the underlying infrastructure and customers protect their data, accounts and configurations. 15-mark preparation for security concerns and challenges in a public cloud , expand sections 4.2, 4.3, 4.4 and 4.5 with examples and the shared responsibility diagram. youtube videos (hindi) abhishek security vision: cloud security cloud. ranchi university mca semester iv, ecmca-401c, 2022–24 paper collection. 5.1 public cloud definition: a public cloud is a cloud environment in which computing resources are provided by a third-party cloud service provider over the internet and made available to multiple customers. example: a company uses amazon web services (aws) to host its website instead of buying its own physical servers. main characteristics: infrastructure is owned and managed by a cloud service provider. resources are shared among multiple customers. services are accessed through the internet. usually needs less initial investment. resources can be scaled according to demand. customers have limited control over the physical infrastructure. examples: aws, microsoft azure, google cloud. 5.2 private cloud definition: a private cloud is a cloud environment dedicated to a single organization. its infrastructure may be managed by the organization itself or by a third-party provider. example: a bank maintains a dedicated cloud environment for confidential customer records and financial information. main characteristics: infrastructure is dedicated to one organization. greater control over resources. security policies can be customized. higher initial investment in many deployments. greater control over infrastructure configuration. suitable for strict security and compliance requirements. public cloud private cloud customer a customer b customer c shared infrastructure owned by the provider, logically separated customers one organization dedicated infrastructure used by one organization only, more control and customization figure: public cloud (shared) vs private cloud (dedicated) 5.3 difference between public cloud and private cloud this comparison table is the most important part of your exam answer. basis public cloud private cloud definition cloud services provided to multiple customers cloud infrastructure dedicated to one organization ownership generally owned by a cloud service provider owned by the organization or a third party infrastructure shared, with logical separation between customers dedicated to a single organization cost generally lower initial investment generally higher setup and maintenance costs security control customer controls its configurations and data, less control over physical infrastructure greater organizational control over security policies and infrastructure customization may be limited by provider services greater customization possible scalability easily scalable using provider resources scaling may need additional dedicated capacity maintenance provider maintains the underlying infrastructure managed by the organization or its selected provider accessibility usually through the internet private networks, or the internet with suitable controls suitable for startups, small businesses, general applications banks, government organizations, specific security requirements 5.4 advantages and disadvantages public cloud advantages low initial investment. easy scalability. no need to buy physical servers. the provider handles physical infrastructure maintenance. resources can be accessed from different locations. disadvantages less direct control over physical infrastructure. dependence on the service provider. security and privacy need careful configuration. internet connectivity may affect access. private cloud advantages greater control over infrastructure. customizable security policies. dedicated resources for one organization. greater flexibility in configuration. useful for specific compliance requirements. disadvantages higher setup costs in many cases. maintenance can be expensive. needs skilled it professionals. scaling may need additional investment. 5.5 conclusion public cloud and private cloud are two important cloud deployment models. public cloud provides shared services with lower initial investment and easy scalability, whereas private cloud provides dedicated infrastructure with greater organizational control and customization. an organization selects the model according to its budget, security requirements, control needs and business objectives. cloud as a service. 7.1 what does gamut of cloud solutions mean? the word gamut means a complete range or variety. gamut of cloud solutions is the wide range of services and solutions that cloud computing offers to individuals and organizations. instead of buying and managing all it resources, organizations use cloud solutions according to their requirements. 7.2 main types of cloud solutions cloud solutions iaas infrastructure paas platform saas software staas storage daas desktop xaas anything figure: gamut of cloud solutions 1. infrastructure as a service (iaas) computing infrastructure such as virtual machines, servers, storage and networking. example: amazon ec2. 2. platform as a service (paas) a platform to develop, test and deploy applications. example: google app engine. 3. security tools analytics tools for analysing large amounts of data a business can host its website, store customer information, manage databases and analyse sales data without building its own one-time reading previous-year question check the supplied collection has no direct question on principal technologies. keep it concise, but do not skip it. 8.1 what are principal technologies? the main technologies that make cloud computing possible. cloud providers combine several technologies to deliver servers, storage, databases and applications over the internet. example: when you upload a photo to google drive, many technologies work together behind the scenes to store it and make it available on different devices. 8.2 major technologies used in cloud computing cloud technologies virtualization distributed computing web services and apis soa networking data centre multi-tenancy automation and orchestration storage security figure: principal technologies behind cloud computing these are important supporting technologies, an explanatory list and not a verbatim syllabus list. virtualization: one physical server runs multiple virtual machines. example: separate virtual servers for different customers. distributed computing: divides work among multiple computers connected through a network. example: many machines process large amounts of data. web services and apis: let software applications communicate over a network. example: an application uses a provider’s api to create a virtual machine. service-oriented architecture (soa): organizes software into independent, reusable services. example: separate payment, user-management and delivery services. networking and internet technologies: high-speed networks connect users to cloud data centres. data centre technology: physical servers, storage, networking equipment, power and cooling systems. multi-tenancy and resource pooling: many customers share physical infrastructure with logical separation. automation and orchestration: automation performs tasks automatically, orchestration coordinates multiple automated tasks. example: a platform creates a vm when a customer requests one. storage technologies: store and manage files, databases and backups. example: cloud object storage for photos and videos. security technologies: authentication, authorization, encryption, firewalls and monitoring. 8.3 how these technologies work together user requests a service web services and apis cloud infrastructure (virtualization + storage) service ready with security and monitoring figure: how technologies work together 8.4 quick revision remember these four technologies from the tutorialspoint explanation: virtualization. service-oriented architecture (soa). grid computing. utility computing. youtube videos principal technologies of cloud computing, hindi. open youtube search sources geeksforgeeks: virtualization and its role in cloud computing. tutorialspoint: cloud computing , cloud computing technologies page (virtualization, soa, grid computing, utility computing). w3schools.in: cloud computing (virtualization, soa, infrastructure tutorials, no page titled principal technologies). topic 9. cloud strategy red red priority : study thoroughly priority note marked red for exam preparation. the supplied question collection has no separate direct question on cloud strategy , so cover the meaning, the main points and the diagram carefully. 9.1 what is a cloud strategy? a cloud strategy is a plan made by an organisation to decide how it will use cloud computing to achieve its business and it goals. before moving applications, data or servers to the cloud, it decides: why does it need cloud computing? which applications should move to the cloud? which cloud model should it choose? how much will it cost? how will it protect its data? how will it manage and monitor cloud services? example: a college wants to move its student-management system to the cloud. it plans the budget, selects a provider, decides how to migrate student data and sets security rules. this planning is its cloud strategy. 9.2 main components of a cloud strategy cloud strategy business goals cloud model selection cloud service selection cost planning security and compliance migration planning monitoring and management figure: main components of a cloud strategy business goals: what the organisation wants to achieve (lower it cost, better performance, growth). cloud model selection: public, private, hybrid or community cloud. cloud service selection: iaas, paas or saas. cost planning: estimate storage, computing, networking and support expenses. security and compliance: protect data, control access, meet legal or regulatory requirements. migration planning: how existing applications, databases and files move to the cloud. monitoring and management: performance, availability, resource usage and costs. 9.3 basic steps for developing a cloud strategy 1. identify requirements 2. assess infrastructure 3. select models and services 4. plan security and budget 5. migration roadmap 6. monitor and optimise figure: steps for developing a cloud strategy identify requirements: understand business and it needs. assess existing infrastructure: check servers, applications, databases and networks. select cloud models and services: choose suitable deployment and service models. plan security and budget: set security policies and estimate costs. prepare a migration roadmap: decide what to move, when and how. monitor and optimise: check performance, security and expenses after adoption. 9.4 why is cloud strategy important? helps achieve business goals. controls unnecessary cloud expenses. improves security and risk management. helps select suitable cloud services. makes migration more organised. supports future business growth. 9.5 cloud strategy vs cloud migration cloud strategy cloud migration overall plan for using cloud process of moving resources to the cloud focuses on business goals and long-term direction focuses on transferring applications and data decides why and where cloud is useful carries out the actual movement remember: cloud strategy is the overall plan that connects business goals, technology choices, security, cost and implementation. youtube videos cloud strategy in hindi. open youtube search sources geeksforgeeks: aws cloud adoption framework and migration strategies gartner and infosys cloud strategy and adoption guidance (consistent with the steps above). topic 10. cloud design and implementation using soa red red priority : 15-mark question, study thoroughly previous-year question status marked red for exam preparation. the compiled collection includes this 15-mark question: explain cloud design and implementation using soa. it is a related question, not confirmed as a direct question from the primary 2022–24 mca semester iv paper. listed under unit ii-b: cloud as a service. 10.1 introduction to soa soa stands for service-oriented architecture . it is a software architectural approach in which an application is divided into independent, reusable services. each service performs a specific business function and communicates with other services through well-defined interfaces, commonly apis. an online shopping application can have: authentication service: login and registration. payment service: processes payments. product service: manages products. order service: manages orders. notification service: sends notifications. 10.2 soa architecture diagram consumers layer cloud service consumers browser (human users) enterprise service bus (esb) providers layer account service book service order service shipping service database database figure: soa architecture: consumers, esb, provider services and databases (bookstore example) 10.3 what is cloud design and implementation using soa? designing an application using soa principles and deploying its services on cloud infrastructure. two separate concepts: soa: defines how an application is divided into independent services and how they communicate. cloud computing: provides virtual machines, storage, databases and networks to run those services. example: an organisation develops authentication, payment and order services and deploys them on cloud servers instead of buying and maintaining physical servers. 10.4 components of soa service: an independent software component that performs a particular task. service provider: creates and provides services to other applications. service consumer: requests and uses services from the provider. service registry: stores service information so consumers can discover available services. 10.5 publish, find, bind model service registry (stores service info) service provider (creates services) service consumer (uses services) 1. publish 2. find 3. bind (use the service) figure: publish, find, bind model of soa publish: the service provider publishes information about its service. find: the service consumer searches for the required service. bind: the consumer connects to and uses the service. 10.6 principles of soa soa principles loose coupling reusability interoperability service abstraction autonomy discoverability figure: principles of soa loose coupling: services have minimum dependency on each other. reusability: a service can be reused by multiple applications. interoperability: services built with different technologies can communicate. service abstraction: internal implementation details are hidden. autonomy: each service controls its own functionality. discoverability: services can be discovered using descriptions or registries. 10.7 steps in cloud design and implementation using soa identify requirements: understand the business requirements of the application. identify services: divide the application into independent services. define interfaces: specify how services communicate and exchange information. develop services: develop or integrate the required services. deploy on cloud: deploy services using cloud infrastructure. enable communication: connect services using apis and communication protocols. apply security: implement authentication, authorization and encryption. monitor services: monitor performance, availability and resource usage. 10.8 benefits of soa in cloud computing reusability: services can be reused by different applications. scalability: individual services can be scaled according to demand. flexibility: services can be modified independently. cost reduction: existing services are reused instead of rebuilt. interoperability: different technologies can communicate. easy maintenance: independent services are easier to maintain. 10.9 example an online shopping application on cloud infrastructure. when a customer buys a product: authentication service verifies the customer. product service provides product details. order service creates the order. payment service processes the payment. notification service sends confirmation. all services communicate through apis and run using cloud resources. 10.10 conclusion soa helps developers design applications using independent, reusable services, while cloud computing provides the infrastructure to deploy and run them. together they help organisations build flexible, scalable and manageable cloud-based applications. exam preparation for 15 marks, prepare the definition, components, publish-find-bind model, principles, implementation steps, benefits, example and a labelled diagram. youtube videos cloud design and implementation using soa, hindi. open youtube search topic 11. conceptual cloud model black black priority : one-time reading previous-year question check the supplied collection has no direct question on the conceptual cloud model. official section: unit ii-b, cloud as a service. 11.1 what is a conceptual cloud model? a high-level representation of how cloud computing works, showing its major components, participants, services and their relationships. it explains: who provides cloud services? who uses them? how are they delivered? what are the service layers? who manages security and auditing? it explains the overall structure without focusing on a particular company’s technology. the nist cloud computing reference architecture is a recognised example. 11.2 the five actors cloud consumer cloud provider saas software paas platform iaas infrastructure resource abstraction and control layer physical resources (servers, storage, network) security and privacy apply across all layers cloud service management: provisioning, portability cloud broker cloud auditor cloud carrier (network connectivity) figure: conceptual cloud model: five nist actors 1. cloud consumer a person or organisation that uses cloud services. example: a company using aws virtual machines, or a student using google drive. 2. cloud provider an organisation that provides cloud services to consumers (aws, microsoft azure, google cloud). it manages the infrastructure and delivers iaas, paas and saas. 3. cloud broker an intermediary between consumers and providers. it helps select, combine or manage services from different providers. three functions: service intermediation: adds value to an existing service, such as identity management. service aggregation: combines multiple cloud services into one solution. service arbitrage: selects services dynamically from different providers based on requirements. 4. cloud auditor independently examines cloud services and operations: security, privacy, performance and compliance. example: an auditor checks whether a provider follows the required security standards. 5. cloud carrier provides the network connection through which services travel from provider to consumer. example: an internet service provider. 11.3 internal layers of the cloud provider a. service layer: iaas, paas, saas b. resource abstraction and control layer c. physical resource layer d. cloud service management figure: internal layers of the cloud provider a. service layer: iaas, paas and saas. b. resource abstraction and control layer: manages and controls underlying resources using virtualisation and resource allocation. c. physical resource layer: servers, storage devices, network equipment and data centre facilities. d. cloud service management: business support, provisioning and configuration, portability and interoperability. security and privacy are cross-cutting concerns across the provider’s architecture. 11.4 how does the model work? a company wants cloud storage: the company is the cloud consumer. it selects a cloud provider. the cloud provider offers storage services. the cloud carrier provides internet connectivity. a cloud broker may help compare or manage services. a cloud auditor may independently check security and compliance. the provider manages its physical resources, service delivery and security. 11.5 importance better understanding: explains the overall structure of cloud computing. role identification: identifies the responsibilities of different actors. service understanding: shows how iaas, paas and saas fit into the provider architecture. security awareness: shows the importance of security and privacy. service management: shows how services are delivered and managed. standardisation: a common reference for discussing and comparing cloud architectures. 11.6 conceptual cloud model vs soa conceptual cloud model soa describes the overall cloud computing structure describes how software is organised into services identifies cloud actors and their roles identifies service providers, consumers and registries explains cloud service delivery explains service communication and reuse focuses on cloud architecture focuses on application architecture 11.7 quick revision five actors: cloud consumer, cloud provider, cloud broker, cloud auditor, cloud carrier. three service models inside the provider: iaas, paas, saas. youtube videos (hindi) prof. jayesh umre: cloud computing reference model in hindi. open youtube search sources nist cloud computing reference architecture (authoritative reference). w3schools.com: aws cloud computing and appml architecture (related architecture concepts, not the complete nist model). topic 12. cloud service defined black black priority : heading is black, but the service models are important previous-year questions why detailed? the heading cloud service defined is marked black, but your compiled collection contains actual previous-year questions on iaas, paas and saas, so the service models get detailed attention. official section: unit ii-b, cloud as a service. 12.1 what is a cloud service? a computing resource or application made available to users over a network, usually the internet, by a cloud service provider. instead of buying and maintaining all computing infrastructure, users access services from companies such as aws, microsoft azure and google cloud. examples: online storage (google drive), cloud servers (aws ec2), application platforms (google app engine), online software (microsoft 365). the three major service models: iaas, paas, saas. saas software as a service ready-to-use software gmail paas platform as a service build and deploy applications google app engine iaas infrastructure as a service servers, storage, networking amazon ec2 figure: iaas, paas and saas with examples 12.2 understanding the three models to build and run a website there are three ways to use cloud services: iaas: the provider gives virtual servers, storage and networking. you manage the operating system, runtime, application and data. paas: the provider gives a platform to develop and run applications. you mainly focus on your code and data. saas: the provider gives ready-to-use software. you simply use the application. 12.3 iaas: infrastructure as a service definition: a cloud service model in which a provider offers fundamental computing resources such as virtual machines, storage and networking over the internet. the provider manages the physical infrastructure; the customer manages the operating system, applications and data. what iaas provides: virtual machines (install your own operating system). storage for files and databases. networking: virtual networks, ip addresses, connectivity. load balancers: distribute incoming traffic across servers. firewalls: help control network access. example: aws ec2. to host a website: create a virtual machine, select an operating system such as ubuntu, install python and libraries, deploy your application, configure networking and security. the provider manages the physical server; you manage the operating system and application. advantages: no physical servers to buy; resources increase or decrease as required; control over the operating system; pay for what you use; suitable for websites and custom applications. examples: aws ec2, microsoft azure virtual machines, google compute engine. 12.4 paas: platform as a service definition: a cloud service model that provides a ready-made environment for developers to build, test, deploy and manage applications without managing the underlying infrastructure. the provider manages servers, operating system, runtime and development environment. what paas provides: operating system management, language runtimes, development tools, web servers, database integration, deployment tools, infrastructure management. example: google app engine. for a fastapi web application, without paas you would create a server, install ubuntu and python, configure the web server, install dependencies, deploy and maintain it. with paas the provider handles most of this; you mainly provide your code and configure deployment. advantages: developers focus on code; less infrastructure management; faster development; deployment and development tools; supports scaling; easier collaboration. examples: google app engine, heroku, azure app service. 12.5 saas: software as a service definition: a cloud service model in which a provider delivers ready-to-use software applications over the internet. users access it through a browser or application. the provider manages the infrastructure, platform, application maintenance and updates. what saas provides: ready-to-use software, online access, software updates, application maintenance, data storage and management, user management features. example: gmail. open gmail, sign in, compose an email, send it. you do not install or manage the email server, operating system or infrastructure; google manages the service. advantages: no software infrastructure to install or maintain; accessible from different devices; automatic updates; easy collaboration; subscription or usage-based access; less local it maintenance. examples: gmail, microsoft 365, salesforce, google workspace, dropbox. 12.6 iaas vs paas vs saas feature iaas paas saas full form infrastructure as a service platform as a service software as a service provides virtual infrastructure application development platform ready-to-use software main users it administrators and developers application developers end users control high medium limited provider manages physical infrastructure infrastructure and platform infrastructure, platform and application customer manages os, applications and data application and data usage and application configuration example aws ec2 google app engine gmail easy way to remember: iaas: you rent a computer. paas: you rent a ready-made development environment. saas: you use ready-made software. 12.7 who manages what? (responsibility diagram) layer iaas paas saas application customer customer provider data customer customer provider runtime customer provider provider middleware customer provider provider operating system customer provider provider virtualization provider provider provider physical servers provider provider provider storage and network provider provider provider customer manages provider manages figure: who manages what in iaas, paas and saas \* in saas, the provider manages the application and underlying service, while customers still manage their accounts, access permissions and use of the data. exact responsibility varies by provider. main concept: moving from iaas to paas to saas, the provider manages more of the technology and the customer manages less. 12.8 how iaas, paas and saas work together saas: ready-to-use software (email, collaboration, crm) used by employees and end users paas: development platform developers build and deploy the shopping application iaas: virtual machines, storage and networks figure: how iaas, paas and saas work together a company building an online shopping application: employees use email, collaboration and crm software (saas); developers build and deploy the shopping application (paas); virtual machines, storage and networks support it (iaas). these are different service models, not three compulsory stages. an organisation can use one, two or all three. 12.9 actual previous-year questions red, 15 marks q1. explain the different service models of cloud computing with suitable examples. red, 15 marks q2. differentiate between paas and iaas. how can a third party manage saas? the paas/iaas and third-party saas wording is in the supplementary 2021–24 ca (dse-2) paper, not the primary 2022–24 mca semester iv paper. yellow, 5 marks q3. explain the different service models of cloud computing. 1 mark the primary 2022–24 mca semester iv paper asked: expand saas. expand iaas. expand paas. do not confuse these with the separate 15-mark questions. 12.10 answer: third-party saas management difference between paas and iaas paas iaas provides a development platform provides virtual infrastructure provider manages os and runtime customer manages os and applications mainly used by application developers used by developers and it administrators less infrastructure control more infrastructure control example: google app engine example: aws ec2 how can a third party manage saas? a third-party saas management provider or managed service provider (msp) helps an organisation manage its saas applications. third-party saas manager user management access control security management integration monitoring backup and recovery cost management compliance figure: what a third-party provider (msp) does for saas user management: create, update and deactivate user accounts. access control: assign permissions and control who can access applications. security management: monitor security settings and help protect accounts. integration: connect different saas applications with each other. monitoring: monitor application availability and performance. backup and recovery: help manage backup and recovery arrangements where supported. cost management: monitor subscriptions, licences and unnecessary expenses. compliance: help follow security and regulatory requirements. example: a company uses microsoft 365. it hires a third-party it management company to manage employee accounts, permissions, security settings, licences and support. the third party manages the organisation’s use of saas; microsoft still operates and maintains the service itself. 12.11 quick revision model remember iaas rent infrastructure paas use a development platform saas use ready-made software full forms: iaas infrastructure as a service, paas platform as a service, saas software as a service. youtube videos (hindi) m prashant: what is cloud computing? 1-mark question on it are confirmed in the primary ranchi university mca semester iv paper (2022–24), and more questions are in the compiled question collection. how much depth: detailed preparation. be ready for 1-mark, 5-mark and 15-mark answers. 1.1 what is a cloud ecosystem? a cloud ecosystem is a collection of different participants, technologies, services and infrastructure that work together to provide and use cloud computing services. in simple words, cloud computing does not work through one company or one technology alone. different organisations and components work together to deliver cloud services to users. example: when you store a file in google drive: google provides the cloud storage service. you act as the cloud consumer. internet connectivity helps you access the service. data centres and servers store your files. security mechanisms protect your account and data. other service partners may support billing, auditing or management. all these participants and components together form a cloud ecosystem. 1.2 main components: the five actors the cloud ecosystem includes five major participants. these five actors are defined in the nist cloud computing reference architecture. cloud consumer cloud service provider cloud broker cloud auditor cloud carrier cloud consumer uses services student / company cloud service provider iaas infra paas platform saas software servers • storage networks • data centres physical resources cloud auditor independent assessment cloud broker intermediary cloud carrier network connectivity and data transport (isp / telecom) use via audit service use audit check figure 1.1: the five actors of the cloud ecosystem (simplified from the nist reference architecture). remember: this is the diagram to practise for your 15-mark answer. it is a simplified study diagram. it does not show every communication path. 1.3 the five actors in detail a. cloud consumer a cloud consumer is a person or organisation that uses cloud services provided by a cloud service provider. example: a student using google drive to store notes, or a company using aws to host its website. main responsibilities: select suitable cloud services. use cloud resources. manage user accounts and access. pay for services according to the agreement. follow the provider's usage and security policies. b. cloud service provider (csp) a cloud service provider is an organisation that makes cloud services available to consumers over a network. examples: amazon web services (aws), microsoft azure, google cloud. a csp provides three major service models: iaas (infrastructure as a service), paas (platform as a service) and saas (software as a service). main responsibilities: provide cloud infrastructure. manage servers, storage and networking. provide cloud applications and platforms. maintain service availability. implement security controls. monitor and manage cloud resources. c. cloud broker a cloud broker acts as an intermediary between cloud consumers and cloud service providers. it helps consumers select, combine and manage cloud services from different providers. example: a company wants to use aws for computing and microsoft azure for another service. a cloud broker can help coordinate and manage these services. three important functions of a cloud broker: service intermediation: adds extra value to an existing cloud service, such as identity management or security monitoring. service aggregation: combines multiple cloud services into one integrated solution. service arbitrage: selects services dynamically from different providers based on price, performance or requirements. cloud consumer company cloud broker service intermediation adds identity / monitoring service aggregation combines services into one service arbitrage picks by price / performance aws azure google cloud figure 1.2: what a cloud broker does between a consumer and several providers. d. cloud auditor a cloud auditor is an independent person or organisation that examines cloud services and operations. its purpose is to check whether cloud services follow required security, privacy and performance standards. main responsibilities: conduct security audits. check privacy protection. evaluate service performance. check compliance with standards and agreements. example: an independent auditor examines whether a cloud provider follows the required security controls. e. cloud carrier a cloud carrier provides the network connectivity and transport through which cloud services are delivered from the provider to the consumer. in simple words, it provides the communication path between the cloud provider and the user. example: an internet service provider or telecom operator that connects your computer to aws or google cloud. main responsibilities: provide network connectivity. transfer data between consumers and providers. maintain network availability. support reliable communication. 1.4 how does the cloud ecosystem work? consider a company that wants to host its website using aws. the company acts as the cloud consumer. aws acts as the cloud service provider. the company may use a cloud broker to compare and manage cloud services. a cloud auditor may independently check security and compliance. a cloud carrier provides the network connection between the company and aws. aws uses servers, storage, networking and data centres to deliver the requested services. broker (optional): compare + manage 1 company consumer 2 network carrier isp / telecom 3 aws provider 4 data centre servers, storage networks cloud auditor independent check figure 1.3: a company hosts its website on aws. every actor has a part to play. thus, all these actors work together to provide cloud computing services. 1.5 difference between the five actors actor main responsibility example cloud consumer uses cloud services company using aws cloud provider provides cloud services aws, azure cloud broker manages / intermediates services multi-cloud service manager cloud auditor independently checks services security auditor cloud carrier provides network connectivity internet or telecom provider 1.6 other technical components apart from the five actors, the ecosystem also depends on several technical components. these support the ecosystem, while the five actors describe the main roles played by different participants. component purpose cloud infrastructure provides computing resources such as servers and networks. virtualization creates virtual versions of physical resources. cloud storage stores files, databases and backups. cloud applications provides software to users over the internet. apis and web services allow different applications and services to communicate. security mechanisms protect data, applications and infrastructure. management tools monitor resources, usage, performance and billing. 1.7 role of a cloud service provider in the ecosystem the cloud service provider is one of the most important actors because it delivers cloud services to consumers. its major functions: infrastructure management: manages physical servers, storage and networking. service delivery: provides iaas, paas and saas. resource management: allocates computing resources according to customer requirements. security management: protects infrastructure, applications and customer data. service monitoring: monitors performance and availability. billing and metering: measures resource usage and charges customers. customer support: helps customers resolve technical problems. 1.8 advantages of a cloud ecosystem resource sharing: different users can access shared cloud infrastructure. scalability: resources can increase or decrease according to demand. cost efficiency: organisations can reduce the need to purchase and maintain physical infrastructure. flexibility: consumers can choose different cloud services. better collaboration: different participants can work together to deliver services. security and auditing: auditors and providers help assess and improve security. easy access: cloud services can be accessed through network connections. 1.9 important terms term meaning cloud ecosystem participants, technologies, services and infrastructure working together to provide and use cloud services. cloud stakeholder an actor in the ecosystem: consumer, provider, broker, auditor or carrier. csp cloud service provider, such as aws, azure or google cloud. service intermediation a broker adds value to an existing service. service aggregation a broker combines several services into one. service arbitrage a broker picks services from different providers by price or performance. 1.10 exam preparation previous-year questions marks question business process management red why study this topic it appeared as a 15-mark question in the primary ranchi university mca semester iv paper (2022–24, ecmca-401c). how much depth: detailed preparation. learn the 15-mark answer well, and be ready for the two 1-mark questions from the compiled collection. 2.1 first understand: what is a business process? a business process is a sequence of related tasks or activities performed by an organisation to achieve a specific goal. example: when a customer purchases a product online, the business follows a process: customer places an order. payment is checked. product availability is checked. product is packed. product is shipped. customer receives a delivery notification. all these connected activities form an order-processing business process. other examples of business processes: employee recruitment, customer registration, bank loan approval, hospital appointment booking, invoice generation and payment. 2.2 what is bpm? bpm stands for business process management . it is a systematic approach used to design, execute, monitor, analyse and improve business processes. in simple words, bpm helps an organisation manage its work in an organised and efficient way. example: a bank loan approval process. a customer submits a loan application. the bank verifies the documents. the credit department checks the customer's eligibility. the manager approves or rejects the loan. the customer receives the final decision. bpm helps organise and manage these steps so that the work is completed properly and efficiently. main activities of bpm process design: plan how the business process should work. process execution: perform the planned activities. process monitoring: track the progress of activities. process analysis: identify delays, errors and bottlenecks. process improvement: make changes to improve performance. 1 design plan steps 2 execute do the work 3 monitor track steps 4 analyse find delays 5 improve make changes repeat: continuous improvement figure 2.1: the five main activities of bpm. improvement feeds back into design. 2.3 what is cloud bpm? cloud bpm (cloud business process management) is the use of cloud-based software and services to design, execute, monitor and improve business processes. in traditional bpm, an organisation may need to install and maintain bpm software on its own servers. in cloud bpm, the bpm software is hosted on cloud infrastructure and accessed through the internet or a network. example: a company uses a cloud-based workflow system to manage employee leave applications. employee submits a leave request. the system sends it to the manager. the manager approves or rejects it. the system updates the leave record. the employee receives a notification. the company does not necessarily need to maintain its own bpm servers. traditional bpm bpm software installed locally own servers, own upkeep organisation manages most infrastructure cloud bpm bpm software hosted in cloud provider-managed cloud infra accessed over internet / network figure 2.2: traditional bpm and cloud bpm. the software is the same idea; where it runs is different. 2.4 difference between traditional bpm and cloud bpm traditional bpm cloud bpm software is generally installed on local infrastructure. software is hosted on cloud infrastructure. organisation manages much of the infrastructure. cloud provider manages the underlying cloud infrastructure. higher initial infrastructure investment may be required. often lower initial investment. access may depend on the organisation's network setup. can be accessed remotely through an internet connection, subject to permissions. scaling may require additional hardware and configuration. resources can generally be scaled more easily. organisation handles software and infrastructure maintenance responsibilities. provider may handle platform maintenance, depending on the service model. 2.5 main components of cloud bpm process modelling and design: creates a visual representation of a business process and defines the order of tasks and decision points. example: designing a loan approval workflow. workflow engine: executes the designed workflow, assigns tasks to the appropriate people or departments, and moves the process from one step to another. process integration: connects the bpm system with other applications. example: connecting an order system with a payment gateway and inventory database. process monitoring: tracks the progress of business processes and shows pending, completed and delayed tasks. process analytics: analyses process performance and helps identify bottlenecks and inefficiencies. security and user management: controls who can access or perform particular tasks. supports authentication, permissions and access control. 2.6 how does cloud bpm work? example: online order processing in an e-commerce company. order received: the customer places an order through the website. payment verification: the bpm workflow sends the payment request for verification. inventory checking: the system checks whether the product is available. packing and shipping: the workflow assigns tasks to the warehouse and delivery team. customer notification: the customer receives an order and delivery update. monitoring and improvement: the company checks processing time, delays and errors. 1 order received customer orders online 2 payment check payment is verified 3 inventory check is product available? 4 pack + ship warehouse, delivery 5 notify customer delivery update 6 monitor time, delays, errors cloud bpm software coordinates all six steps figure 2.3: cloud bpm workflow for an online order. the software coordinates all six steps. the cloud bpm software coordinates these activities and helps the organisation track the entire process. 2.7 why is cloud bpm software needed? important: this is the most important part of the 15-mark question. reduced infrastructure cost: an organisation may not need to purchase and maintain its own servers for bpm software. this can reduce initial infrastructure investment. accessibility: employees and managers can access the bpm system from different locations through an authorised network connection. scalability: when the organisation grows or the number of business processes increases, cloud resources can generally be scaled according to demand. better collaboration: employees, managers and different departments can work together on the same business process. process automation: repeated manual tasks, such as sending approval requests and notifications, can be automated. real-time monitoring: managers can track process progress, pending tasks, delays and performance. easy integration: cloud bpm can connect with other business applications, such as databases, payment systems, crm and erp software. faster deployment: cloud-based bpm environments can be made available without first building and maintaining all the supporting it infrastructure. ibm describes its bpm-on-cloud offering as a paas environment for developing, testing, running and monitoring processes. improved productivity: automation reduces repetitive work and allows employees to focus on more important activities. continuous improvement: by analysing process performance, organisations can identify bottlenecks and improve their workflows. 2.8 advantages and challenges of cloud bpm advantages challenges lower initial infrastructure cost dependence on network connectivity access from different locations data privacy and security concerns easier scalability dependence on the cloud provider automation of repetitive tasks integration with older systems can be difficult better process monitoring migration and employee training may take time easier collaboration service availability and vendor dependency must be considered remember: cloud bpm does not automatically guarantee security or uninterrupted service. organisations still need suitable access controls, data protection, backups and service agreements. 2.9 important terms term meaning bpm business process management cloud bpm cloud-based business question. how much depth: study the concepts and prepare a 5-mark answer. 3.1 what is cloud service management? first understand the two words: cloud service: a service delivered through cloud computing, such as virtual machines, cloud storage, databases or online software. management: controlling, monitoring and maintaining something so that it works properly. cloud service management (csm) refers to all the functions needed to manage and operate cloud services that are provided to cloud consumers. in simple words: cloud service management means managing cloud services throughout their operation so that customers receive the services they require with the expected quality. example: a company uses aws to host its website. someone must manage customer accounts, service contracts, resource provisioning, performance monitoring, usage measurement, billing and service availability. these activities come under cloud service management. the nist cloud computing reference architecture describes three major perspectives of cloud service management: business support, provisioning and configuration, and portability and interoperability. 3.2 three major components of cloud service management important: this is the most important concept in this topic. cloud service management 1 business support customer management contract management inventory accounting and billing reporting and auditing 2 provisioning / config rapid provisioning resource changes monitoring metering sla management 3 portability / interop data portability bulk data transfer service interoperability vm migration application migration figure 3.1: the three components of cloud service management (simplified from the nist reference architecture). a. business support business-related activities required to manage customers and support cloud service operations. customer management: manages customer accounts and profiles, handles customer relationships and resolves customer problems and queries. example: creating and managing an aws customer account. contract management: manages agreements between cloud providers and customers, including contract creation, negotiation and termination. example: managing a customer's cloud service agreement. inventory management: maintains information about available cloud services and manages the service catalogue. example: a list of available virtual machines, databases and storage services. accounting and billing: records customer usage, calculates service charges, generates invoices and manages payments. example: calculating monthly charges based on virtual machine usage. reporting and auditing: generates reports about service usage and customer activities, and helps examine service operations and maintain records. b. provisioning and configuration manages the creation, configuration and operation of cloud services and resources. rapid provisioning: quickly provides cloud resources according to customer requirements. example: creating a virtual machine when a customer requests one. resource change: allows resources to be modified when requirements change. example: increasing a virtual machine's memory or cpu capacity. monitoring and reporting: tracks the condition and performance of cloud services. example: monitoring cpu usage and service availability. metering: measures how much of a cloud service a customer uses. example: storage consumption in gb or virtual machine running time. sla management: monitors whether the cloud provider meets the service commitments agreed with the customer. example: checking whether the service meets its agreed availability target. c. portability and interoperability these functions help customers move data, applications and services between different cloud environments and work with different systems. data portability: move data from one cloud environment to another. example: moving files from one cloud storage provider to another. copy data to-from: copy data between cloud systems or between a cloud and another environment. bulk data transfer: transfer large amounts of data efficiently. service interoperability: different cloud services and systems communicate and work together. example: connecting a cloud application to a cloud database. unified management interface: a common interface for managing different cloud services. system portability: move systems or workloads between environments. vm image migration: move virtual machine images between supported environments. application/service migration: transfer applications or services to another cloud environment. these functions are particularly useful when an organisation wants flexibility and does not want to become unnecessarily dependent on one cloud provider. 3.3 how cloud service management works example: a company wants to create a virtual machine on a cloud platform. customer request: the company requests a virtual machine with specific cpu, memory and storage. business support: the provider manages the customer account, service agreement and billing details. provisioning and configuration: the provider creates and configures the virtual machine. monitoring and sla management: the provider monitors the service and checks whether it meets the agreed service levels. usage measurement and billing: the provider measures resource usage and calculates the charges. portability: if required and technically supported, the customer can move data or workloads to another environment. 1 request vm: cpu, ram, storage 2 business support account + billing 3 provision + set up create the vm 4 monitor + sla check service levels 5 meter + bill measure use, charge 6 portability move data if needed management covers the service from request to operation figure 3.2: cloud service management from the first request to ongoing operation. this shows how cloud service management supports a cloud service from the customer's request through its ongoing operation. 3.4 cloud service management vs resource management these two terms are related, but they are not exactly the same. cloud service management resource management focuses on managing services delivered to customers. focuses on managing the underlying it resources. handles service contracts, provisioning, billing and slas. handles physical servers, storage, networks and virtual resources. concerned with service delivery and quality. concerned with resource availability and utilisation. example: managing a customer's virtual machine service. example: managing the physical server hosting that virtual machine. service management contracts, provisioning, billing, slas resource management servers, storage, networks, virtual resources runs on figure 3.3: service management handles what the customer receives. resource management handles the infrastructure behind it. easy way to remember: service management = managing what the customer receives. resource management = managing the infrastructure used to provide it. the itu cloud computing management reference also distinguishes the service management layer from the resource management layer. 3.5 important functions: quick a cloud stack is a collection of technology layers and components that work together to provide cloud computing services. in simple words, a cloud stack describes how cloud services are organised, from the physical hardware at the bottom to the applications used by customers at the top. example: when you use google drive: physical servers store your files. virtualisation helps share computing resources. cloud infrastructure provides storage and networking. the platform supports the application. google drive provides the software interface you use. these layers work together as a cloud stack. 4.2 layers of the cloud stack application layer · saas gmail, drive, salesforce platform layer · paas runtime, databases, dev tools infrastructure layer · iaas virtual machines, storage, networks virtualisation layer hypervisors, vms, abstraction physical resource layer servers, storage, network, data centres closest to user hardware service layer resource abstraction + control layer physical resource layer figure 4.1: the layers of a simplified cloud stack. the nist view groups them into three layers (right). note: this is a simplified teaching diagram. actual cloud-provider architectures can combine or separate layers differently. the nist reference architecture describes a provider stack using three main layers: service layer, resource abstraction and control layer, and physical resource layer. the service layer contains saas, paas and iaas. 1. physical resource layer the bottom layer. it contains the actual physical resources required to run cloud services: physical servers, storage devices, network equipment, data centres, and power and cooling facilities. 2. virtualisation layer creates virtual versions of physical resources: virtual machines, virtual storage, virtual networks and hypervisors. it helps multiple customers share physical resources while maintaining logical separation. 3. infrastructure layer (iaas) iaas stands for infrastructure as a service. it provides computing infrastructure through cloud services: virtual servers, cloud storage, virtual networks and computing resources. example: amazon ec2. 4. platform layer (paas) paas stands for platform as a service. it provides a platform where developers can build, test and deploy applications without managing all the underlying infrastructure: application runtime environments, development tools, managed databases and middleware. 5. application layer (saas) saas stands for software as a service. it provides ready-to-use software applications over a network. examples: gmail, google drive, microsoft 365, salesforce. 4.3 how do the layers work together? example: a developer wants to deploy a website. the physical layer provides servers, storage and networking. the virtualisation layer creates virtual machines. the infrastructure layer provides computing resources. the platform layer provides the runtime and development environment. the application layer delivers the website to users. this is how different layers cooperate to deliver a cloud application. 4.4 difference between iaas, paas and saas model what it provides example iaas computing infrastructure amazon ec2 paas application development platform google app engine saas ready-to-use software gmail remember: iaas provides infrastructure, paas provides a platform, and saas provides software. 4.5 why is cloud stack important? organisation: divides cloud technology into manageable layers. resource utilisation: helps share and use physical resources efficiently. scalability: makes it easier to expand cloud resources. flexibility: different layers can be managed or updated independently. service delivery: helps providers deliver different types of cloud services. 4.6 important terms term meaning cloud stack collection of cloud technology layers working together hypervisor software that creates virtual machines from physical resources iaas / paas / saas infrastructure, platform and software as a service middleware software that connects applications and services in a platform 4.7 exam preparation 1-mark answer a cloud stack is a collection of technology layers that work together to provide layers are: physical resource layer: contains physical servers, storage devices, networks and data centres. virtualisation layer: creates virtual machines, virtual storage and virtual networks. infrastructure layer (iaas): provides virtual computing resources, storage and networking. platform layer (paas): provides tools and environments for application development and deployment. application layer (saas): provides ready-to-use applications over a network. thus, the cloud stack organises the technologies required to deliver cloud computing services. 15-mark preparation extend demand? computing on demand (cod) means getting computing resources whenever they are needed, instead of buying and maintaining all the resources permanently. these resources can include: computing power: cpu and ram. storage: space to store files and databases. networking: network bandwidth and connectivity. software: applications and development platforms. the user requests resources when shopping website. on normal days, 2 servers are enough. during a festival sale, thousands of customers visit your website. you temporarily increase the number of servers to handle the traffic. after
